author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A Merrimack County judge is considering a lawsuit seeking to remove a proposed New Hampshire school tax cap from the November ballot. Superior Court Judge Dan St. Hilaire heard arguments over whether the question gives voters a clear explanation of the change they are being asked to approve.

The challenge was brought by Campton school board member Kelly Wieser and Warner taxpayer David Bates. They contend the wording is confusing and does not adequately describe how the cap would operate. The state argues that lawmakers properly enacted the measure and that the plaintiffs do not have legal standing to block it.

If approved by voters, the proposal would limit annual growth in local property-tax levies for schools, with adjustments tied to inflation and new construction. It would also place a 6% limit on growth in school administrative-unit central-office spending. Timing is tight because ballot printing is expected to begin late next week. St. Hilaire indicated that a decision would come quickly, giving election officials and local governments little room for delay before ballots are finalized.
dek: A superior court judge is expected to rule quickly as ballot printing approaches for the proposed school spending and tax limits.
headline: Judge weighs challenge to New Hampshire school tax-cap ballot question
